subject: FintechAI — pricing & latency trade-offs (post-call follow-up)
messages:
From: Julia Park <julia.park@fintechai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: FintechAI Procurement <procurement@fintechai.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: FintechAI — Redwood pricing follow-up & throughput/latency Qs

Marissa / team,

Thanks again for the call earlier — helpful overview of Redwood's serving options. Quick recap from our side and a few follow-ups so we can shape budget and next steps: 

- Primary workload: real-time scoring + short conversational summaries for customer support.
- Expected traffic: 150k requests/day initially, trending to ~750k/day over 6 months.
- Average tokens: prompt ~140 tokens, response ~220 tokens (~360 tokens per request).
- Peak burst: up to 350 qps for <5 minutes during batch jobs/alerts.
- Latency SLO: p95 target ~200ms for interactive flows, higher OK for async backfills.
- Budget: trying to put a numbers box on this — we have a monthly budget target in the $30k–$75k range for model inference (incl. embeddings, classification).

Could you send a short post-call note with: 1) expected $/1M tokens for Hosted vs Dedicated (ballpark), 2) which tier you'd recommend for our latency SLO & burst profile, and 3) options for mixing streaming vs batching to hit cost targets?

I attached a quick CSV with projected volumes over the next 12 months (estimated-usage.csv). Procurement looped in on Cc for timing and procurement questions.

Thanks — happy to hop on another call if easier.

Best,
Julia
Julia Park
Head of ML Platforms, FintechAI
julie.park@fintechai.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@fintechai.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FintechAI — Redwood pricing follow-up & throughput/latency Qs

Julia — thanks for the clear recap and the CSV. Looping in Nikhil (SE) and Neha (AM) so we can align on a concise economic model and next steps.

Post-call recap + clarifying Qs:
- You mentioned ~360 tokens per request on average. Is that representative for both interactive and async jobs, or do async backfills tend to be larger?
- For p95=200ms, is that required for all endpoints or only the customer-facing chat flow?

Quick answers up front, we'll follow with a short pricing sheet (attached):
- Ballpark hosted pricing: $180–$260 / 1M tokens for the model class we discussed (varies by model and streaming vs non-streaming).
- Ballpark dedicated/reserved pricing: $45–$90 / 1M tokens depending on committed capacity and quantization/profile. Dedicated gives you more predictable p95 and lower unit cost at scale.

Latency vs cost trade-offs (short):
- Streaming (token-by-token) + small batch sizes: best for interactive SLOs (p95 ~80–100ms depending on model/hardware) but higher per-token unit cost because you lose batching efficiency.
- Aggressive batching: can reduce per-token cost by 2–5x at the cost of added queuing latency (not ideal for p95=200ms interactive flows).
- Hybrid approach: route customer-facing requests to a low-latency pool (smaller batch sizes, streaming enabled) and route async/summarization jobs to a cost-optimized batch pool.

Suggested next steps:
1) We (Nikhil + I) will run a quick unit-economics calc based on the CSV you sent and return a one-page with Hosted vs Dedicated projected $/1M numbers and a starter config recommendation.
2) If the numbers look good, we can scope a short pilot (4–6 weeks) on Dedicated reserved or Hosted with burst.
3) Procurement: please share any standard contract terms or timeline constraints so we can surface to Legal.

Attached: redwood-pricing.xlsx (ballpark numbers + starter configs). Will follow up with a short call invite if helpful.

- Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com

From: Julia Park <julia.park@fintechai.com>

Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 08:31:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FintechAI — Redwood pricing follow-up & throughput/latency Qs

Thanks Marissa — quick answers:
- Async backfills are larger (~1.2k tokens/request) for the most part; interactive stays near the 360 tokens you used.
- The 200ms p95 is only for the chat/support flow (customer-facing). Other endpoints can accept higher latency.
- Budget: procurement can commit to a pilot in the $30k/month range and would consider expansion if unit economics look favorable. Target internal threshold is $/1M tokens <= $100 for the long-term.
- Timeline: procurement review and PO by end of August would be ideal.

Let us know the ballpark economics and recommended starter tier, and we'll try to schedule procurement/technical alignment next week.

Best,
Julia

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@fintechai.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, FintechAI Procurement <procurement@fintechai.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FintechAI — Redwood pricing follow-up & throughput/latency Qs

Julia — great, thanks for the clarifications and the target threshold. High-level economics and recommended starter configuration below (ballpark, will formalize in a quote):

Unit economics (ballpark, normalized to 1M tokens):
- Hosted (Standard tier, streaming-enabled): $220 / 1M tokens. Typical p95: 150–350ms depending on model and concurrent load. Good for fast time-to-value and minimal operational overhead.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pool, baseline commit + burst): $60 / 1M tokens at ~1–3M tokens/day commit; deeper discounts ($45/1M) start above sustained commit tiers (~20M tokens/month). Typical p95: 60–140ms with proper sizing and KV cache warm.

Latency vs cost guidance:
- For your customer-facing chat (p95 ~200ms): recommend a small Dedicated pool or a higher-tier Hosted instance with streaming enabled. Dedicated will hit your <$100/1M target at scale and provide more predictable latency for bursty QPS.
- For async backfills (1.2k tokens/request): push to a cost-optimized batch pool (Dedicated lower-priority nodes or Hosted batch windows) — batching here reduces unit cost significantly.
- Hybrid routing: we can automatically route by route name/priority so you get low-latency for chat and cost-efficient execution for backfills.

Operational notes:
- Batching settings: small batch size (4–8) for interactive streaming; large batch sizes (64–256) for backfills.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: streaming better for perceived latency (users see tokens earlier) but slightly higher cost in Hosted due to fewer batching gains; on Dedicated you can tune kernels to reduce that penalty.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Nikhil will produce a 1-page unit-economics table based on your CSV and return a Hosted vs Dedicated proforma by EOD tomorrow.
2) We'll attach a draft SLA and a pilot statement of work (SLA-DRAFT-FintechAI.pdf).
3) If procurement wants it, I can introduce our Pricing Ops lead for committed tiers and contracting details.

Attaching: SLA-DRAFT-FintechAI.pdf. HubSpot deal created: https://hubspot.com/deals/4831.

If that looks good we can lock a pilot and outline the PO timeline for August.

Thanks — Marissa
